issues.legal_issue: A landowner’s conduct did not amount to waiver, estoppel, or acquiescence barring a suit to recover possession from trespassers.
material_facts: The defendants occupied the land as trespassers and did not establish that they had acquired a right in it from an owner or had authority to use it on the owner’s behalf.
After learning of the trespass, the owner sent written notices objecting to it and asserted his rights within a reasonable time.
The owner did not stand by while the defendants constructed valuable permanent structures; the structures were tin sheds and fittings that could be removed.
There was no evidence that the owner encouraged the defendants to incur expense or represented that they could remain on the land.
issues.conclusion: Waiver, estoppel, and acquiescence did not bar the owner’s suit for possession.
issues.legal_principle: The principles governing estoppel and acquiescence require facts bringing the case within the established equitable doctrines; the court found no encouragement or representation inducing a detrimental change of position and no standing by while valuable constructions were made. The court relied on Ariff v. Jadunath Majumdar, A.H. Forbes v. Sir L.E. Ralli, Ahmed Tar Khan v. Secretary of State for India in Council, Lala Beni Ram v. Kundan Lall, Subodh Chand Mitter v. Bhagwandas Saha, Ramsden v. Lee Dyson and Joseph Ithornton, and Willmott v. Barber.

rule.if: eviction_suit_against_trespassers and (no_owner_representation_inducing_reliance and no_owner_encouragement_of_detrimental_expense) and owner_objected_after_learning_of_trespass and owner_did_not_stand_by_while_valuable_permanent_structures_were_built and trespassers_acquired_no_right_from_an_owner

predicates.eviction_suit_against_trespassers: The proceeding is a suit by a landowner to recover possession from people occupying the land as trespassers.
predicates.no_owner_representation_inducing_relianc: The landowner made no representation that induced the occupants to change their position to their disadvantage.
predicates.no_owner_encouragement_of_detrimental_ex: The landowner did not encourage the occupants to incur expense on the land.
predicates.owner_objected_after_learning_of_trespas: The landowner objected to the occupation after learning of it.
predicates.owner_did_not_stand_by_while_valuable_pe: The landowner did not watch without objection while the occupants built valuable permanent structures.
predicates.trespassers_acquired_no_right_from_an_ow: The occupants did not acquire a right to the land from an owner.

issues.definition: When a landowner seeks possession from trespassers, made no representation or encouragement inducing detrimental reliance, objected after learning of the trespass, did not stand by during construction of valuable permanent structures, and the occupants acquired no right from an owner, the suit is not barred by waiver or estoppel.

issues.legal_issue: A prior suit does not bar a later suit under the rule against splitting claims when the suits arise from different causes of action.
material_facts: Earlier suits concerning the defendants’ use and occupation of the land ended in compromise decrees.
The defendants did not carry out the terms of those compromise decrees.

The cause of action in the suit for possession was different from the causes of action in the compromised suits, and the failure to comply with the compromise terms formed part of the later suit’s cause of action.
issues.conclusion: The rule against splitting claims did not bar the suit for possession.
issues.legal_principle: Order 2, Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not apply where the later suit arises from a cause of action different from those in the earlier suits; failure to perform the compromise decrees formed part of the cause of action in the later suit.

predicates.later_suit_after_prior_compromised_suits: The proceeding is a later suit brought after earlier suits between the parties ended in compromise decrees.
predicates.causes_of_action_are_different: The later suit and the earlier suits arise from different causes of action.
predicates.nonperformance_of_prior_compromise_terms: A party’s failure to perform the earlier compromise terms forms part of the cause of action in the later suit.

issues.definition: When a later suit follows prior compromised suits, arises from a different cause of action, and includes nonperformance of the prior compromise terms as part of its cause of action, the later suit is not barred by the prior suits.
